instructions: Compare the U-Proof KNOWN benchmark run (agent_benchmark_report@1 - agents had access to real prior Creative Touch project knowledge/audit history for U-Proof) against the Imvusa BLIND benchmark run (blind_benchmark_report@1 - agents had ONLY approved doctrine, no project-specific prior knowledge, genuinely new site). Score exactly these 7 dimensions, each with a uProofAssessment, imvusaAssessment, and verdict: independent_discovery_quality (how much real, non-obvious discovery happened without prior knowledge to lean on - Imvusa is the harder test of this since it had zero project history); generic_vs_site_specific (did findings actually reference real, specific site details - phone numbers, page names, duplicated content, price figures - versus generic boilerplate advice that could apply to any site); hallucinations (did any stage invent facts, pages, prices, competitors, or credentials not traceable to real evidence - be specific about any found in either run, or state none found); implementation_specificity (how concrete and actionable was build_plan in each run); visual_reasoning_quality (both runs disclosed no real vision input - assess how honestly and usefully that limitation was handled in each); seo_reasoning_quality (content_pack quality, honesty about the business model - ecommerce for U-Proof vs lead-gen for Imvusa); qa_challenge_quality (how substantively did Stage 6 QA actually challenge prior stages in each run - compare the real defects found). Then give an overall trustRecommendation (TRUST / TRUST_WITH_CONDITIONS / DO_NOT_TRUST_YET) for whether this CT-OS pipeline, run for real via Gemini-preferred/Claude-fallback (later Claude-only) providers, could be trusted on a third, unseen client site, with explicit conditions. Also note in overallFindings any real infrastructure/provider-reliability observations from running this benchmark: Gemini hit a real HTTP 429 daily quota exhaustion partway through and never recovered for the rest of the session; Claude (claude-sonnet-5) then carried the entire remainder of both pipelines; Claude's forced tool-use output was observed to occasionally emit malformed XML-style <parameter> tags inside string fields on the first attempt for two different jobs, resolved by an explicit anti-XML instruction and/or retry; Claude's default output-token cap (originally 4096, hardcoded in the adapter with no env override) was too small for larger schemas and had to be raised. IMPORTANT OUTPUT FORMAT NOTE: return each field as plain JSON values directly as the tool-call argument. Do not emit any XML-style <parameter name=...> tags anywhere in your output, including inside string or array values.

content.businessUnderstanding: The pipeline correctly understood that U-Proof is a South African waterproofing/building-products manufacturer (owner Martin) whose WooCommerce ecommerce site is being rebuilt/completed by Creative Touch after a prior developer relationship ended without handover. It correctly captured that the client likes the existing design and wants completion/improvement rather than a redesign, that real VAT-inclusive ZAR retail pricing was supplied and must be used exactly (Liquid Rubber, Fibre Filler, Wall & Roof Paint, Zinc Phosphate Primer, Bonding Liquid Primer, Plaster Primer, Membrane), and that the client wants live Fastway Courier shipping rates plus Payflex BNPL/card payment rather than manual EFT or flat-rate shipping as the primary checkout path. It also correctly treated this as a non-blind run, cross-referencing Creative Touch's own prior 2026-09-02 technical audit rather than starting fresh.
audienceInferred: South African contractors purchasing waterproofing materials for commercial/residential jobs
DIY homebuilders sealing roofs, walls, foundations and cracks
Architects/specifiers needing technical validation before specifying products
Trade buyers seeking bulk/technical pricing via phone contact
content.conversionModelInferred: Primary model is direct ecommerce purchase through WooCommerce: browse by category or application use-case -> view accurate size/variant pricing (5L/20L, membrane widths) -> add to cart -> checkout with live Fastway Courier shipping rate calculation -> pay via Paystack card or Payflex BNPL (explicitly avoiding EFT/manual/COD as primary). A secondary, lower-volume conversion path is trade/technical lead generation via phone or contact form for architects and bulk buyers.

content.businessUnderstanding: The pipeline correctly identified Imvusa Furniture as a real South African custom furniture, reupholstery, and interior services business operating from two physical locations (George and Bloemfontein), not an ecommerce retailer. It recognized that the absence of shop/cart/checkout/pricing pages is appropriate and expected for a custom-quote services business rather than a defect to fix, and it correctly identified the business's fabric supplier partnership (Hertex Fabrics) and named fabric collections (ADORN, CAPPADOCIA, COASTLINES, ESQUIRE) as real content to preserve and correct, not invent.

content.conversionModelInferred: Lead-generation / consultation model: the site's core conversion action is a prospective client submitting a quote or consultation request (or calling/visiting a location), not completing an online purchase. The blueprint formalizes this into a single canonical conversion funnel (a dedicated Get a Quote flow) fed from Services, Gallery, and Leather Couches pages, backed by one authoritative Contact Block per location — appropriate for custom, individually-quoted work with no published pricing.

knowledge.title: Every build passes through the safety pipeline
knowledge.content: BUILD -> PREVIEW -> HUMAN DESIGN APPROVAL -> QA -> FINAL REGRESSION AUDIT -> CONTROLLED ACTIVATION TESTING -> HUMAN LAUNCH APPROVAL -> LIVE. No stage may be skipped by an agent.

knowledge.title: GREEN / AMBER / RED permission tiers
knowledge.content: GREEN actions run automatically. AMBER actions require explicit human approval before execution. RED actions (DNS, registrar, payment credentials, destructive infrastructure) are never executed by an agent without explicit, named authorization.

knowledge.title: Launch never auto-approves
knowledge.content: QA at zero is necessary, never sufficient, for launch. Launch requires human approval; approving with open launch holds is a deliberate, recorded human decision.

knowledge.title: Agents propose; humans approve knowledge
knowledge.content: Agents may propose lesson candidates. No agent may promote its own output into AGENCY or DOCTRINE knowledge. Human approval is the only path from CANDIDATE to APPROVED.

knowledge.title: U-Proof prior Creative Touch audit history (as of 2026-09-02)
knowledge.content: Creative Touch's own prior hands-on technical audit history for this project (most recent pass 2026-09-02): no shipping zones/methods configured (test order confirmed silent no-shipping checkout, since deleted); only BACS/Cheque/COD enabled, Paystack/Payflex installed but never configured with real credentials; compiled Shop/Product/Cart/Checkout build files were found hardcoding a third-party 10Web trial domain (allowed-pony.10web.cloud) for logo/breadcrumb/footer/payment-icon assets, confirmed live and customer-facing as of 2026-09-02, then stripped from on-disk build files in a housekeeping pass (not independently re-verified live since); a fake 'recent articles' teaser section (FAQs, How to Apply Liquid Rubber, Surface Preparation Guide) on the homepage links to non-existent pages, left from an earlier AI-generated clone; real broken homepage CTA links were found and fixed; a placeholder-style phone number pattern (+27100000000) was noted; WooCommerce shipping-origin address was corrected to match the Contact page's address at the time (Unit 4, Gateway Industrial Park, Sebenza, Edenvale, Johannesburg); order-notification emails were going to Creative Touch's own address rather than the client's business inbox, and the outgoing from-address was a leftover third-party domain - both flagged, not resolved; security hardening was applied (headers, stripped version-disclosure tags, removed exposed backup files); real Size and Size x Color variation structures were built and verified for Liquid Rubber, Fibre Filler, Wall & Roof Paint and Membrane with real pricing. None of this should be assumed still accurate without checking fresh evidence - several items already appear to have changed.

knowledge.title: U-Proof business context
knowledge.content: The client (Martin) owns a South African waterproofing/building-products company, U-Proof. Creative Touch is rebuilding/completing the company's ecommerce website on WordPress + WooCommerce after a prior developer relationship broke down without a proper handover. The client likes the existing design and wants it completed and improved, not redesigned. The client does not want manual/flat-rate shipping and prefers live courier rates (Fastway Couriers); Payflex (SA buy-now-pay-later) was under evaluation alongside a standard card gateway, because the client does not want EFT/manual payment as the primary path.
